original.text: yathaiva viṣatattvajño viṣamālokya bhakṣayan | kevalaṃ muhyate nāsau rogamuktaśca jāyate ||
original.edition: Cittaviśuddhiprakaraṇa, GRETIL/DSBC e-text (IAST by the unit)
original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: As one who knows the truth of poison eats poison seeing it for what it is and is not merely stupefied but becomes free of disease, (so the yogin enjoys objects).

original.text: bālā rajyanti rūpeṣu vairāgyaṃ yānti madhyamāḥ | svabhāvajñā vimucyante rūpasyottamabuddhayaḥ ||
original.edition: Cittaviśuddhiprakaraṇa, GRETIL/DSBC e-text (IAST by the unit)
original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: Fools are attached to forms, the middling go to dispassion, and those of highest understanding, knowing the nature of form, are liberated.

original.text: yena yena hi bandhyante jantavo raudrakarmaṇā | sopāyena tu tenaiva mucyante bhavabandhanāt ||
original.edition: Cittaviśuddhiprakaraṇa, GRETIL/DSBC e-text (IAST by the unit)
original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: By whatever violent deeds beings are bound, by those very deeds, joined with means, they are freed from the bonds of existence.
